# WebRiskAudit

> WebRiskAudit is an open-source, non-commercial passive security scanner. Given a domain, it runs a small set of automated checks against publicly visible signals and summarizes them in a score from 0 to 100. Results are heuristic and are not a substitute for a professional security assessment.

- Website: https://webriskaudit.com
- Source code: https://github.com/portakalp/webriskaudit
- Author: Taha Gökalp Bakar (https://github.com/portakalp)
- Cost: free to use. Nothing is sold and there are no paid plans.

## What it checks

- Email authentication: SPF record, DKIM record on common selectors, DMARC record.
- Reputation: whether the domain's IP address is listed on public DNS blocklists.
- TLS: whether the certificate is valid and not expiring within 30 days.
- HTTP: presence of five security headers (Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Permissions-Policy, Referrer-Policy), whether the Server header discloses software, and whether a CDN or WAF is detected.
- Privacy: whether a privacy policy page can be found.

## How it works

- Only passive checks are performed: DNS lookups, one TLS handshake and a few ordinary HTTP GET requests.
- No port scanning, crawling, fuzzing, authentication or exploitation is attempted.
- No account is needed. The domain is sent to the WebRiskAudit API, which runs the checks and returns the result without storing it.

## Limitations

- Results are automated and heuristic. Some checks give the benefit of the doubt when a request times out, and some signals (for example DKIM selectors or CDN detection) can be missed.
- A high score does not mean a site is secure, and a low score does not mean it is compromised.
- It is not a penetration test, a vulnerability assessment or legal or compliance advice.

## Pages

- https://webriskaudit.com/ : scan form and report
- https://webriskaudit.com/privacy-policy : privacy note
